title: State and evolution of data analytics infrastructure at ESOC
organisation: European Space Agency, European Space Operations Centre (ESOC); published by The Aerospace Corporation with permission (GSAW 2020)
status_notes: Slide deck dated 03/03/2020 (title slide, PDF p. 1). Marked 'ESA UNCLASSIFIED - For Official Use' on every slide and '© 2020 by European Space Agency. Published by The Aerospace Corporation with permission'.
summary:
A short ESOC slide deck from GSAW 2020 on the off-line data analytics infrastructure that sits beside the mission control systems. It sets out a generic big-data layering (raw, processing, optimised and speed layers) and maps ESOC's tools onto it. **ARES** (Analysis and Reporting System) provides storage and infrastructure. PyARES, the (deep) novelty detection system, the Dependency Finder and long-term data preservation (LTDP) products and collections provide data accessibility.

ARES is an off-line analysis system that evolved from ESA's MUST (Mission Utility Support tools) and is built on the EGOS User Desktop framework. It mainly stores spacecraft housekeeping data in engineering format, and also files, parameters and events, optimised for fast retrieval. The architecture slide shows ARES importing [EDDS](../scos2000/edds.md) response files on its own LAN. EDDS in turn draws on the MCS [archives](../scos2000/archives.md) (DARC, PARC) on the OPS-LAN. The deck motivates a multi-mission shared big-data store with Gaia's volume (around 150 million unique HKTM samples per day). It describes PyARES as a Python library for retrieval and user-defined or machine-learning processing on Spark/HBase/Protobuf. Novelty Detection and the Dependency Finder are AI tools for spotting unusual telemetry behaviour and statistical dependencies between parameters; the Dependency Finder was validated by the Mars Express flight control team. The LTDP prototype combines ARES, Elasticsearch and a REST API. Future work listed includes processing live TM streams, migrating legacy missions to Hadoop and building a curated anomaly-detection dataset.

Infrastructure: (Big Data) Multi mission shared storage

key_points.text: The big-data architecture has a raw layer (full fidelity, file/folder structures), a processing layer (distributed computation), an optimised layer (structured, organised by consumer use case) and a speed layer (low latency).
At ESOC, ARES provides storage/infrastructure, while PyARES, the Novelty Detection system, Dependency Finder and LTDP products and collections provide data accessibility.
ARES (Analysis and Reporting System) is an off-line data analysis system that evolved from ESA's Mission Utility Support tools (MUST) and is built on the EGOS User Desktop framework (EUD).

ARES mainly stores spacecraft housekeeping data in engineering format, supports generic storage of files, parameters and events, and imports EDDS response files; the diagram shows EDDS reaching the MCS archives (DARC, PARC) on the OPS-LAN.
Gaia receives around 150 million unique HKTM samples per day, which is used to motivate a multi-mission shared big-data storage.

PyARES is a Python library for ARES metadata and data retrieval, user-defined-function processing and machine-learning jobs (Random Forest), bringing processing to the data with PySpark over Spark, HBase and Protobuf.
The Dependency Finder prototype was developed by the Artificial Intelligence & Operations Innovation Team and validated by the Mars Express Flight Control Team.
The LTDP products and collections platform was prototyped with ARES (Hadoop database cluster), Elasticsearch and a RESTful API.
